CRITICAL INCIDENT ALERT: production-db-primary
Timestamp: 2026-09-22T03:15:22Z
Source: Datadog APM & AWS CloudWatch
Service: pg-cluster-primary.us-east-1 (Aurora Postgres 15.4)
Metric Alarm: DatabaseConnectionPoolExhausted
Details: Active connections spiked to 498/500 (99.6% capacity). Log snippet: 'FATAL: remaining connection slots are reserved for non-replication superuser connections'.
Impact: Upstream service 'checkout-api' reporting 38.4% HTTP 500 failure rate. P99 latency rose from 120ms to 14,850ms. 45 container pods in CrashLoopBackOff due to failed database health checks.
Blast Radius: Global checkout pipeline blocked; customer transactions failing at gateway step.

severity.instructions: Determine the operational incident severity tier (P4 low to P1 critical).
criteria: P4 - Low: Cosmetic issue, minor internal inconvenience, or non-blocking bug with negligible customer impact.
P3 - Medium: Degraded non-critical service or partial internal tooling outage with an immediate workaround available.
P2 - High: Severe degradation of major customer-facing features, high latency, or partial production outage affecting multiple tenants.
P1 - Critical: Complete system outage, catastrophic core workflow failure, active data loss, or severe security breach requiring emergency bridge.

team.instructions: Select the engineering domain team that owns primary resolution of this alert.

criteria.backend: Application business logic, microservice APIs, payment processing workflows, and backend service code.
criteria.frontend: Web application client UI, mobile apps, styling/CSS layout, JavaScript bundles, and browser compatibility.
criteria.security: Unauthorized access, suspicious auth geography, credential stuffing, vulnerability exploit, or data breach.
criteria.infrastructure: Cloud platforms (AWS/GCP), Kubernetes clusters, database engines/connection pools, VPC networking, and bare metal.
criteria.data: Data warehouse pipelines, ETL jobs, streaming Kafka topics, and analytical reporting models.

is_customer_facing.instructions: Does this incident directly impact external customer transactions, client UI availability, or public user experience?
